title: Somewhere Along the Way, We Stopped Doing These Things Simple rules we all learned once and should bring back
author: Chris Martin
source: The Ways of a Gentleman (Martin Substack), January 27, 2026
summary: Martin catalogs a series of simple social courtesies and practices that have fallen away from modern culture—practices like writing thank-you notes, maintaining proper posture, dressing intentionally, greeting neighbors by name, looking people in the eye during conversation, and finishing what we start. He argues that these are not nostalgic affectations but practical wisdom about how to live with dignity and respect. Each of these small practices reinforces character, signals respect to others, and contributes to a social fabric that has been noticeably weakened by their abandonment. Martin calls for their revival not as a return to the past but as a recognition that these practices serve real purposes: they build community, strengthen relationships, and allow individuals to carry themselves with confidence and grace.
points: Simple social courtesies like thank-you notes, eye contact, proper posture, and intentional dress have fallen away, but their loss has weakened both character and social fabric.
Each of these practices, though small, reinforces character, signals respect, and contributes to community and connection in ways modern shortcuts cannot replace.
Writing a thank-you note teaches attentiveness; maintaining posture teaches self-respect; dressing intentionally teaches that we care about the world we enter and the people we'll meet.
These practices are not nostalgic affectations but practical wisdom about how to live with dignity—they serve real psychological and relational purposes.
Revival of these practices is not a return to the past but recognition that they allow individuals to carry themselves with confidence, grace, and genuine respect for others.
